feedback.Physical Object: Excluded — The certificate is a symbolic legal record, not defined by its physical instantiation.
feedback.Synthetic: Included — A formal human-invented document standardized by legal systems.
feedback.Biological/Biomimetic: Excluded — Refers to a biological event but is not biologically inspired in structure.
feedback.Powered: Excluded — Not mechanically or electronically powered.
feedback.Structural: Excluded — Not a load-bearing or architectural structure.
feedback.Observable: Excluded — The document can be read or viewed, but observability is incidental.
feedback.Physical Medium: Excluded — May be printed or digital, but functionally independent of medium.
feedback.Active: Excluded — Requires institutional context to have meaning.
feedback.Intentionally Designed: Included — Created as an official record-keeping and identity-establishing mechanism.
feedback.Outputs Effect: Excluded — Enables access and verification, but does not emit output autonomously.
feedback.Processes Signals/Logic: Excluded — Holds data, but does not perform signal processing or logical computation.
feedback.State-Transforming: Excluded — Establishes legal status but does not autonomously enact change.
feedback.Human-Interactive: Excluded — Read and referenced, but not interacted with functionally.
feedback.System-integrated: Excluded — Used within systems, but not an operational module.
feedback.Functionally Autonomous: Excluded — Requires institutional recognition and use.
feedback.System-Essential: Excluded — Some societies function without formal birth registration systems.
feedback.Symbolic: Included — Symbolizes entry into society, legal identity, and civic status.
feedback.Signalling: Included — Serves as a signal of legitimacy, legal existence, and familial/legal affiliation.
feedback.Rule-governed: Included — Must adhere to strict legal formats and data standards.
feedback.Compositional: Included — Composed of distinct structured fields (e.g., name, time, location, parentage).
feedback.Normative: Included — Society expects every legal person to possess such a record.
feedback.Meta: Excluded — Does not refer to other records or to its own type.
feedback.Temporal: Included — Anchors identity and eligibility in time (birth date, age).
feedback.Digital/Virtual: Included — Stored and managed in national or institutional digital systems.
feedback.Social Construct: Included — Exists because of shared institutional agreements and civic conventions.
feedback.Institutionally Defined: Included — Defined and issued by governments, hospitals, or registries.
feedback.Identity-Linked: Included — A foundational legal identity artifact for every person.
feedback.Regulated: Included — Subject to legal frameworks, authentication rules, and access control.
feedback.Economically Significant: Included — Needed for financial services, healthcare, education, travel.
feedback.Politicised: Included — Involved in debates over personhood, statelessness, surveillance, and privacy.
feedback.Ritualised: Included — The registration of birth and issuance of certificate constitutes a civic rite.
feedback.Ethically Significant: Included — Raises questions about dignity, access, legal recognition, and equity.

encoding_notes: This encoding treats the birth certificate as a symbolic, compositional, temporally anchored institutional artifact. It plays a foundational role in defining personhood and social inclusion, and is tightly bound to normative, legal, and ethical structures in civic life.
